newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco says Reynolds won't buy plant.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco says Reynolds won't buy plant.

text.p: Australian aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Friday that Reynolds Metals Co had decided not to buy its wheel manufacturing plant, Southern Aluminium, in Tasmania.
Southern Aluminium said in a statement that Comalco would have no alternative but to close the plant, which makes wheels for domestic and overseas car manufacturers.
Southern Aluminium general manager David Sadler said in a statement he was extremely disappointed the sale had fallen through, but gave no reason for Reynolds's decision.
"It would have been more economic to close the plant earlier," he said, but added that the company had hoped the business and its associated employment could continue.
Comalco has declined to disclose the possible sale price or book value of the plant but a spokesman confirmed a newspaper report that the company had invested about A$50 million in it.
The sale would have completed Comalco's programme of selling downstream assets and focusing on its mining, refining and smelting businesses.
Sadler said Comalco had been seeking a buyer for Southern Aluminium for some time and Reynolds had been the last option to secure its future.
Comalco is owned 67 percent by Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd.
